subject.title: feat: support split frontend and API origins

question: Should ClickClack officially support credentialed browser sessions across separately configured frontend and API origins, and may this server contract land before the corresponding OpenClaw version 1 setup-code consumer ships?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but accepting cross-origin cookies/CORS and coordinating a protocol consumed by another repository are security and release-policy choices that source review and CI cannot settle.

options.title: Approve coordinated rollout
options.body: Approve the exact-origin security model and merge or release it together with validated OpenClaw consumer support and end-to-end proof.

options.title: Stage the server contract
options.body: Land the server-side contract but keep split-origin setup explicitly unsupported or gated until the compatible OpenClaw consumer is released.

options.title: Retain same-origin support only
options.body: Defer the credentialed cross-origin deployment model and narrow this work to non-browser setup metadata or reverse-proxy documentation.

recommendation.title: Approve coordinated rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the exact-origin security model and merge or release it together with validated OpenClaw consumer support and end-to-end proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch coordinates the ClickClack server, browser, SDK, documentation, and the required OpenClaw consumer protocol.
